name: Cross Keys Middle School
notes: Refined seed's '1960s?' to probable 1960s: the Wedgwood subdivision HOA history states FFSD acquired the land on which the Wedgwood and Cross Keys schools were later built during the subdivision's construction (fall 1963 - May 1967); a classmates.com listing shows a Cross Keys alumnus from 1968-69 and a 1971 'The Padlock' yearbook for 'Cross Keys Jr. High' (grades 6-9) exists. Exact opening year not found online. Operated as Cross Keys Junior High (grades 6-9) before becoming a middle school. The Missouri Historical Society genealogy index lists an earlier 'Cross Keys School' at New Halls Ferry Road just north of Parker Road - a different site ~1 mi south, likely the rural predecessor school the current campus replaced; that lineage is unverified. FFSD's 2027-28 restructuring plan will convert Cross Keys to a 6-8 middle school (fergflor.org board post). Currently operating at 14205 Cougar Drive.

name: Wedgwood 6th Grade Center
notes: Same land-acquisition evidence as ALL-033: FFSD acquired the Wedgwood school site while the surrounding Wedgwood subdivision was being built (fall 1963 - May 1967), so the school opened in the mid-to-late 1960s; exact year not found. Originally Wedgwood Elementary (K-6); converted to a 6th Grade Center when FFSD reconfigured grades to primary (PreK-2) / intermediate (3-5) / 6th-grade-center / middle (7-8) around 2019-2021 (Wikipedia district article lists it as 'Wedgewood Sixth Grade Center, formerly Wedgwood Elementary School'). Spelling varies: NCES uses 'Wedgwood', Wikipedia and some FFSD materials use 'Wedgewood'. Still operating at 14275 New Halls Ferry Road per NCES (2024-25) and the FFSD 2023-24 directory.

name: Commons Lane Elementary School
school_type: Public Primary School (PreK-2; formerly K-6 elementary)
notes: Currently operating at 2700 Derhake Road - listed in the official FFSD 2023-24 building directory and has its own site (clps.fergflor.org, 'Commons Lane Primary School'). Reconfigured from K-6 elementary to a PreK-2 primary school in FFSD's grade-level restructuring; feeding into an intermediate partner (likely Robinwood). Opening year not found in web sources; the surrounding Derhake subdivisions were built in the early-mid 1960s, suggesting a mid-1960s construction, but no citation found - left unknown.

name: Halls Ferry Elementary School
school_type: Public Intermediate School (grades 3-5; formerly K-6 elementary)
notes: Currently operating at 13585 New Halls Ferry Road (FFSD 2023-24 directory; 2018-19 parent handbook at resources.finalsite.net). Now serves grades 3-5 as 'Halls Ferry Intermediate School' after FFSD's grade reconfiguration (Wikipedia district article). Opening year not found online. Note: the Halls Ferry name traces to the 19th-century Hall's Ferry route; a different rural 'Halls Ferry'-area school lineage may exist in the historical record but was not verified.

name: Jury Elementary School
notes: Operating at 11950 Old Halls Ferry Road - listed as school #26 on the official Hazelwood School District map/directory (City of Hazelwood document center) and reported in flovalleynews as an active school in 2009+. Jury is NOT one of the 13 rural schoolhouses that formed Hazelwood SD in 1949-51 (per the district's 150th-anniversary Coldwater School article listing them: Brown, Coldwater, Vossenkemper, Pea Ridge, Columbia Bottom, Prigge, Twillman, Black Jack, Elm Grove, Hyatt, Rosary, Garrett, Bonfils), so it is a post-consolidation building; the 'Jury School' former name suggests it may continue an older rural Jury district/school name, but no founding date found - left unknown.

name: Jamestown Elementary School
notes: Operating at 13750 Old Jamestown Road - NCES status 'Open' (PK-5, NCES ID 291383000626) and school #17 on the official HSD map; school site jam.hazelwoodschools.org. Named for the Old Jamestown community, first documented 1819 (Phenias James advertised 'James' Town' lots; the 1988 Old Jamestown Community Area Study, oldjamestownassociation.org, covers the community history). The school itself is NOT among the 13 schoolhouses that formed Hazelwood SD in 1949-51, so it is a post-consolidation building; opening year not found online - left unknown.

name: Parker Road Elementary School
school_type: Public Primary School (PreK-2; formerly K-6 elementary)
notes: Operating at 2800 Parker Road (FFSD 2023-24 directory). Served K-6 as recently as 2017 (flovalleynews Green Ribbon article mentions sixth-grade girls at Parker Road, May 2017); now a PreK-2 'Parker Road Primary School' under FFSD's grade reconfiguration. Opening year not found online - left unknown.

name: Robinwood Elementary School
school_type: Public Intermediate School (grades 3-5; formerly K-6 elementary)
notes: Operating at 955 Derhake Road (FFSD 2023-24 directory). Now serves grades 3-5 as 'Robinwood Intermediate School' after FFSD's reconfiguration. Opening year not found online - left unknown.

name: Townsend Elementary School
notes: Operating at 6645 Parker Road - school #19 on the official HSD map and its own site (tow.hazelwoodschools.org). Held a 'grand re-opening' on Nov. 24, 2008 after renovations under the Hazelwood 1st facilities program (flovalleynews, Nov. 2008). Not among the 13 original Hazelwood schoolhouses; original opening year not found - left unknown.

name: Ackerman School
district_operator: Special School District of St. Louis County
notes: Seed's 'Unknown' resolved: SSD's own history page states 'In 1961, SSD opened Ackerman School in Florissant [as] the first special education school for the District' (SSD formed December 1957, began classes fall 1958). Still operating at 1550 Derhake Road serving students from Ferguson-Florissant, Hazelwood, Jennings and Riverview Gardens districts (flovalleynews, Aug. 2015; SSD site).

name: Northview High School
district_operator: Special School District of St. Louis County
notes: Operating at 1520 Derhake Road (northview.ssdmo.org). Building history: the previous Northview building was demolished in May 2015 and replaced by a new $30M facility designed by Bond Architects that opened Aug. 31, 2015 after weather delays (flovalleynews, Aug. 2015; bondarchitectsinc.com project page). The school's original founding year was not found online - presumably post-1958 as SSD expanded; left unknown. Serves the same attendance area as Ackerman (FFSD, Hazelwood, Jennings, Riverview Gardens).

name: North Technical High School
district_operator: Special School District of St. Louis County
notes: Seed's 'Unknown' resolved: SSD's official Applied Tech history page states the district moved into technical education in 1966, opened South Technical in 1967, and 'the following year, SSD opened North Technical High School in North St. Louis County' - i.e., 1968. Still operating at 1700 Derhake Road; one of SSD's two tech high schools and the only one enrolling full-time students eligible for athletic participation (flovalleynews, Aug. 2015). Hosts SSD's Applied Tech practical nursing program site. Named a Missouri A+ School in 2015 (ssdmo.org/our-story).

name: East Early Childhood Center
notes: SEED ERROR: the seed's District/Operator ('Special School District/Ferguson-Florissant') is wrong. NCES (ID 291383003208) places East Early Childhood Center in the Hazelwood district, and the official HSD map lists 'ECE East, 12555 Partridge Run' as Hazelwood site #29 - it is Hazelwood's early childhood education center, not an SSD or FFSD facility. Corrected district_operator accordingly. Still open per NCES. Opening year not found - left unknown.

name: Our Lady of Fatima School
historical_names: Our Lady of Fatima Catholic School
district_operator: Our Lady of Fatima Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Parish founded 1950 and the church and school occupied the same building at 4500-50 Washington St. (closedparishes.com, sourcing Archdiocese 'Closed Parishes' records); the school likely opened in the early-mid 1950s - exact year not found, so '1950s' probable. School closed in 2004 (privateschoolreview.com NCES-derived record), one year BEFORE the parish itself closed in 2005. In 2005 the parish was dissolved: territory north of I-270 merged with St. Dismas and St. Thomas the Apostle to form St. Rose Philippine Duchesne Parish; the merged parish's school was placed at the former St. Thomas the Apostle School site - i.e., the school lineage continued at ALL-047, recorded as probable successor (students may also have gone to Blessed Teresa of Calcutta-parish-area schools south of I-270). The property sold for $1.6M in 2005: Johnny Londoff Chevrolet bought the site; Lindenwood University bought the church/school building for its North County campus (archbalt.org, Jan. 2012; flovalleynews, Mar. 2008 - the reuse is the separate seed row ALL-076). The convent at 4450 Washington was later sold to the City of Florissant.

name: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne School
historical_names: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne Catholic School
district_operator: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
opened_citation: Seed NCES-derived value; corroborated by parish/site history at stlouis.closedparishes.com/parish/st-thomas-the-apostle-florissant/
notes: LINEAGE: the school at 3500 St. Catherine Street was originally St. Thomas the Apostle School (St. Thomas the Apostle Parish, founded 1960 - stlgs.org / closedparishes.com). The seed's NCES-derived 1967 opening is consistent with a mid-1960s school build on a 1960-founded parish site but was not independently verified - probable. In 2005 the parish merged with St. Dismas and Our Lady of Fatima (north of I-270) to form St. Rose Philippine Duchesne Parish; Archbishop Burke's announcement specified 'the school for the new parish will be at the current St. Thomas the Apostle School' (STLPR, May 2005), so the school was renamed St. Rose Philippine Duchesne School at that site (confirmed at 3500 St. Catherine in the 2017-18 MNSAA accredited-schools list). In 2018 the school joined St. Ferdinand and St. Norbert schools under the new All Saints Academy governance partnership (St. Louis Review) - recorded here as closed 2018 with successor ALL-048 (All Saints Academy - St. Rose campus, a separate seed row in batch04). That campus itself closed after the 2022-23 school year due to enrollment decline (St. Louis Review, June 2023); the parish was subsumed into Sacred Heart Parish, Florissant, on Aug. 1, 2023 under the 'All Things New' plan. NOTE: ALL-108 (batch05) is a cross-batch duplicate of successor ALL-048.
